repair.content:
Restrict uniqueness to integral_0^1 Phi(t)/t dt > -infinity.

Use the bar in (22), the ratio s=e^-|E|/tau, and negative part in (49). With Omega=E* minus F_tau, int_Omega(u0-tau)_- = e^-|E|-tau+tau|E|-tau|F_tau| = tau(s-log s-1) >= tau(1-s)^2/2. The difference has derivative -(1-s)^2/s<=0 and vanishes at one. In the far branch s<1/2, the remainder is >=tau/8 >=tau D[f]^2/16, since D[f]^2<=2; multiplying by the coherent hinge integral (<=1) preserves the needed bound. The near branch uses the cited Faber-Krahn bound with normalized Fock distance and c0 reduced if necessary.

Insert the uniform factor 1/4 when converting to trace distance, or explicitly rename c after reducing it. Any claim that the original larger numerical coefficient fails would require a separate example, which is not supplied. Theorem 14 may use the same constant as Theorem 1 because D[f]^2<=D[rho]^2; that transfer is an implication.
